long_biography.plain_text:
Cars shaped David MacNeil's working life long before WeatherTech. Raised in the Chicago suburbs by his mother, a pediatric-nursing instructor, he pumped gas, drove taxis and limousines, worked as a machinist and sold cars. He later became vice president of sales at AMG and operated a classic-car dealership, building the product knowledge and dealer relationships that supported his next venture.

A 1989 trip to Scotland supplied the idea: MacNeil noticed rental-car mats designed to contain rain and mud. He secured North American distribution rights and mortgaged his home to finance the first shipment. Demand made the venture profitable within two years. WeatherTech later brought production to the United States, developed laser-measured floor liners and expanded into household and pet products while MacNeil retained full ownership.
